title: i2i self-fix fires on nearly every run when threshold is 9.5
detail: Across 8 scorable i2i runs with autoFix+threshold 9.5, selfFix triggered every time. I2I rarely clears a 9.5 gate first pass; budget the extra fix re-run into expected cost.

title: autoFixThreshold 9.5 is the de-facto default for this workflow
detail: 13 of 15 runs set autoFixThreshold=9.5; only the 2 LoRA self-tests ran without it. Treat 9.5 as the working ceiling to gate against, not a special case.

title: flux2-klein I2I rarely clears 9.5 overall in one pass
detail: Every scored flux2-klein i2i run fell under the 9.5 threshold and triggered self-fix. Expect a single I2I generation to land ~8-9 overall; plan for the fix iteration rather than raising steps pre-emptively.

title: A triggered self-fix does not guarantee a new fix-caption
detail: fixCaptions was 0 on 4 of 8 i2i self-fix runs. The score-gate keeps a fix only if it beats baseline on the target dimension; equal-or-worse fixes produce no caption. Don't read fixCaptions=0 as 'no fix attempted'.

title: If VLM captioning yields 0 images scored, self-fix is skipped entirely
detail: Run 23-21-23 generated 1 image but captionCount=0 and selfFix=false with reviewHtml=false. A caption phase failure (LM Studio down / error) leaves nothing to gate on, so the whole loop no-ops.

title: flux2-klein T2I routinely runs at 4-6 steps
detail: The 3 most recent t2i runs used steps 4-6 with LoRAs (anatomyfix, bodyweight sliders) and passed the gate without self-fix. flux2-klein is a distilled model; 4-6 steps is the working band, not 12+.

title: anatomyfix / bodyweight slider LoRAs at scale 0.7-1.1 improve anatomy without triggering self-fix
detail: Recent t2i runs applied klein_slider_anatomy (1.1) and bodyweight (0.7) and cleared the gate first pass. Slider LoRAs in the 0.7-1.1 band are a low-risk lever for pose/anatomy problems vs raising steps.

title: Multi-spec runs generate sequentially and self-fix is per-batch not per-image
detail: Run 12-16-49 ran 3 specs (2 with LoRAs, different seeds) in one envelope; selfFix=false for the whole batch. Batch mode reports one selfFix flag covering all specs, not one per image.

title: LoRA self-test runs (selfTest:'lora:*') skip the autoFix phase
detail: Both lora:multi-zimage selfTest runs had no autoFix/selfFix and produced 4 captions each (LoRA A/B pairs). LoRA-review self-tests are an A/B comparison lane, not a self-improve lane.

title: i2i runs use mode:'debug' almost exclusively
detail: All scored i2i runs passed mode:'debug'. Debug mode is the working i2i configuration for this workflow; non-debug i2i is untested in history.

title: Feeding exported i2i_feedback JSON into the next run improves source-fidelity iteration
detail: The earliest 4 i2i runs all loaded i2i_feedback_20260614.json (feedback phase) and each still triggered self-fix. Feedback drives prompt/denoise guidance but does NOT pre-clear the 9.5 gate; expect fix iteration even with feedback.

title: A self-fix that lifts a weak target dimension is kept even when overall is flat
detail: The score-gate is dimension-aware: a fix targeting detail/composition/etc. is accepted on strict-greater on THAT dimension. fixCaptions>0 on targeted-dimension runs (13-56-13, 13-33-01, 10-08-37) confirms targeted fixes survive an overall-flat gate.

title: Detail/texture is the dimension i2i self-fix most often targets
detail: i2i self-fix runs that produced a fix-caption (fixCaptions>0) cluster on fine-detail weaknesses (skin pores, fabric) — the classic denoise-vs-detail tradeoff. Detail is the default suspect for an i2i gate miss.

title: Lowering denoise_strength to recover detail trades away prompt_adherence
detail: The documented i2i lever: dn down preserves source detail/clothing but costs style transfer (prompt_adherence drops). When detail is the gate miss, prefer a slider LoRA or +steps over aggressive denoise reduction.

title: Prompt prefix 'anatomyfix,' helps with full-body anatomy/hands on flux2-klein
detail: Recent full-body poses (warrior yoga, arabesque, standing) led with 'anatomyfix,' and 'detailed hands and face' and cleared the gate. Use the anatomyfix prefix as a cheap prompt-side lever before LoRA.

title: All historical runs completed with zero phases_failed
detail: phases_failed is [] across every run; the workflow is reliability-stable. A 'complete' status does NOT mean quality passed — it means the pipeline ran end-to-end (self-fix may still have fired or no-op'd).

title: Review HTML is built whenever captioning succeeds
detail: reviewHtml=true on all runs with captionCount>0; false only when captionCount=0 (23-21-23). The HTML finalize phase is gated on having scored images, not on the run kind.

title: Reusing one seed across count-N yields identical images; vary seed per spec
detail: Best-of-N needs distinct seeds per spec, not one seed with count>1 (that returns [seed]*N overwriting _s{seed}.png). In multi-spec runs, set a different seed per spec (100/200/300 pattern seen in 12-16-49) for real variance.

title: zimage-turbo LoRAs show no quality lift over a strong base
detail: The lora:multi-zimage self-tests ran as A/B comparison (4 captions, no autofix) consistent with the known ceiling effect: base already scores ~9/10 so LoRAs can't differentiate. Use harder prompts to differentiate, not more LoRAs.

title: A single-spec run can pass the gate first pass without self-fix
detail: Eight single-spec runs (2026-06-19T01-17-06, 18-10-11, 18-22-56, 2026-06-20T01-39-09, 03-01-36, 03-26-56, 04-24-28, and 2026-06-20T05-13-51) all finished with selfFix=false, fixCaptions=0, reviewHtml=true. Single-spec runs are the low-cost baseline shape: no batch overhead, no fix iteration, finalize still fires. Contrast with i2i runs that almost always self-fix.

title: prompt_adherence is the dimension that most differentiates image outputs
detail: detail/sharpness/artifacts hover near ceiling (8-10) for both baseline and tuned configs, but prompt_adherence swings 4.75-10. Treat prompt_adherence as the dimension that separates outputs; weight quality gates and self-fix targeting on it. (Migrated from retired workflow mlx-movie-director-lora-review.)

title: Hard prompts collapse the baseline to ~2.6 overall vs ~8.5 on easy prompts
detail: Hard prompts (arabesque, hands, action poses) drop baseline overall to ~2.58 vs ~8.5 on easy prompts. This is where prompt/config changes can genuinely beat the baseline — never judge improvements on easy prompts alone, or every run looks like a 9/10 tie. (Migrated from retired workflow mlx-movie-director-lora-review.)
